# SortByField

Sorts an array of objects by the value of one of their properties.

## Signature

```jyro
# fragment
SortByField(items, fieldName, direction)
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | array | The array to sort, which is left unchanged. Null is read as the empty array; any other type that is not an array is a runtime error. |
| `fieldName` | string | The name of the property to sort by, matched exactly, case included. A number or a boolean is read as its string form, and null as the empty string. |
| `direction` | string | The order: `"asc"` for ascending or `"desc"` for descending, with no case sensitivity for ASCII letters, so `"Desc"` is accepted too. Any other string, null, or a value of another type is a runtime error. |

## Returns

Array. A new array holding the elements of items ordered by the value of fieldName, in the given direction. Never null.

## Remarks

The values are ordered as `Sort` orders them: null first, then booleans, numbers, strings, arrays, objects and functions, never causing an error. An element that is not an object, or an object without the property, sorts as null. The sort is stable: elements whose values compare equal keep their original order.

## Example

`SortByField([{"n": 2}, {"n": 1}], "n", "asc")` returns `[{"n": 1}, {"n": 2}]`.
